title: Inference-Time Steering Across Scaffolds and Epitopes for Sample-Efficient De Novo Nanobody Design
abstract: arXiv:2610.13844v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Generative molecular design typically relies on over-generation and post-hoc filtering. Inference-time steering methods like Feynman-Kac (FK) steering improve efficiency by biasing trajectories toward high-reward candidates, yet they optimize within a single fixed configuration. In de novo nanobody design, upfront commitment to conditioning choices like scaffold identity or target epitope creates a bottleneck. Since yield varies across these conditions, steering unpromising setups wastes compute. We recast generative condition selection as an inference-time resource-allocation problem. We propose two dynamic budget allocators: a joint Global Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) formulation that steers and allocates compute across configurations concurrently, and a decoupled approach adapting Batched Successive Elimination (BaSE). translated_title: 跨支架与表位的推理时引导以实现样本高效的从头纳米抗体设计
translated_abstract: 生成式分子设计通常依赖于过度生成与事后过滤。像Feynman-Kac（FK）引导这样的推理时引导方法通过将生成轨迹偏向高奖励候选来提高效率，但它们只能在单一固定配置内进行优化。在从头纳米抗体设计中，预先确定支架类型或目标表位等条件选择会造成瓶颈。由于产量在不同条件之间差异很大，对没有前景的设置进行引导会浪费计算资源。我们将生成式条件选择重新表述为一个推理时资源分配问题。我们提出了两种动态预算分配器：一种是联合的全局序贯蒙特卡罗（SMC）方法，可以在不同配置之间并发地进行引导和计算资源分配；另一种是改编自批处理逐次消除（BaSE）的解耦方法。实验表明，这些动态分配器将每GPU小时可设计候选的产量提升了近5倍。
tldr: 该论文将纳米抗体设计中的条件选择（支架与表位）重新表述为推理时资源分配问题，提出全局SMC和改编BaSE两种动态预算分配器，使每GPU小时可设计候选产量提升近5倍。
en_tdlr: The paper recasts condition selection (scaffolds and epitopes) in nanobody design as an inference-time resource-allocation problem, proposing two dynamic budget allocators (Global SMC and adapted BaSE) that boost the yield of designable candidates per GPU-hour by nearly 5×.
